speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to begin our evaluation, could you tell me exactly how many days old you are and when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jejunal Atresia.

The combination of bilious vomiting, feeding intolerance starting immediately after birth (6 hours post-delivery), and the maternal history of missed prenatal checkups (which increases the risk of undiagnosed fetal anomalies like polyhydramnios) strongly suggests a proximal intestinal obstruction. The family history of pyloric stenosis is a red herring given the timing, as pyloric stenosis typically presents at 3-6 weeks of life with non-bilious vomiting. The immediate onset points to a congenital obstruction higher than the ampulla of Vater. Please proceed with an Abdominal_X-Ray to look for the "double bubble" sign or distal gas patterns, and prepare for a contrast enema to rule out distal atresia.
